title: The names she is filed under
dek: One woman, six spellings of her maiden surname, three of her forename and four married surnames — and the indexes carry the worst of them.

people.why: Her parents' given names are the oldest unsolved question in this archive. Every route to them runs through an index, and an index can only be searched on a spelling.

forms.where: Most files, and her own 1953 marriage register
forms.note: The form this archive treats as canonical.
The de Witt divorce. French spelling, in an Afrikaans court.
The correct Portuguese spelling, and the one most searches start and stop with.
With the particle. A surname search that anchors on the first letter can miss this.
The fullest form anybody wrote down, and the only record that gives her a second family name. It is the single most important spelling on this page.
An 'e' lost. This is how NAAIRS carries the Salkow divorce, and it is why that file went unfound for months.
Written by a clerk in front of her, with her standing there. Not a transcription error at a distance.
Not Portuguese, not a variant, not anything a person would write. An index corruption — and it is attached to the one file in which SHE is the plaintiff.
Her first marriage. She is still being called this in files from 1951.
The spelling this archive is named for.
With a 'y'. One NAAIRS record only.
An 'e' for an 'i'. This one spelling hid the restitution file for weeks.
The third marriage, over within the year.

forms.where: The NAAIRS index, TAB MHG 7029/54 and KAB PIO 990
forms.note: With a Q. Found 16 September 2026 by testing spellings nobody had written down. NAAIRS files a Johannesburg estate under it that the Union Gazette advertises as FIGUEIREDO — two indexes, two spellings, one man.

forms.where: FamilySearch, South Africa Civil Marriage Records
forms.note: FamilySearch files married names INSIDE the surname field, so she is indexed as one long surname. A search for FIGUEIREDO alone may not reach it.

others.name: Kurt Luwinski
others.note: The same three spellings as his wife's married name, and for the same reason — they come from the same court files.

others.note: Not yet found to vary in any record this archive holds. Listed because the Y-DNA project was searched on all three and the possibility should not be quietly forgotten.

tested_dek: Every form put to every index that could be reached, 16 September 2026. The column that matters is the last one.

tested.unique: The known corpus. Everything below is invisible to it.

THE FIND OF THE DAY. TAB MHG 7029/54 — FIQUEIREDO, AGOSTINHO VICENTE SEBASTIAO, a Portuguese man whose Johannesburg estate the Union Gazette advertises under FIGUEIREDO. Also KAB PIO 990/42707E, IMMIGRATION PAPERS JG DE FIQUEIREDO. Not claimed as kin — but no search on the correct spelling could ever have seen either.
TAB WLD 2545/1950. The only action in which Ivone is the plaintiff. Reachable by no other maiden spelling.
The same file, from the other side of the marriage.
KAB IRC 1/4/19 and IRC 1/3/1 — two immigration files. Neither is hers.
TAB WLD 2225/1953, the Salkow divorce, as NAAIRS spells it.
SAB BAL 7 — a temporary permit for a Goanese C FIGUERDO. A different community, but it proves the permit series is indexed.
One divorce apiece, none connected. Recorded so that nobody searches them twice.

A REAL FAMILY, AND NOT THIS ONE. German-Jewish Johannesburg — Erwin, Bella born Berman, Meinhard, Ingeborg Ursula born Leske. Tested because Kurt came out of East Prussia and the slide from Luwinski to Lewinski is exactly the slide a clerk makes. It did not happen. Recorded as an exclusion rather than left as an open possibility.

tested.form: FIGUERETTO · FIGARETO · FIGUEIRDO · FIGUIREDO · FIGUERREDO · FIGUERIEDO · FIGUEIRETO
tested.unique: Nothing, anywhere. Invented spellings that no clerk ever made.

A REAL MAN, AND NOT OURS. Israel Blogos Lawinski, suing Georg Marthinus Kleynhans in the Transvaal in 1903 — TAB ZTPD 8/678, 888/1903. Twenty-five years before Kurt was born and in the wrong court. Excluded.
Also real, also not ours. Erich Lubinski's estate TAB MHG 4010/73, and Johanna born Schaefer, 1922–1992. No connection offered or found.
Returns the Luwinski set plus nothing new — the stem search is a superset, not a discovery.

NOT SEARCHED THROUGH, and said so plainly. Both are common surnames in their own right rather than misspellings of hers, and both exceeded the harvest cap. Listed so that the gap is visible rather than silently absent — MOTA is one of her recorded names and MOTTA is one letter from it.
